title: Student Portal - HELB
summary: Understanding the HELB Student Portal
content:
Understanding the HELB Student Portal

The Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) provides a dedicated online portal for students to manage their loan accounts and access essential services. As a State Agency under the Ministry of Education, HELB uses this platform to facilitate direct interaction between the board and its loanees.

What is the Student Portal?

The Student Portal acts as a centralized digital hub for Kenyan university, college, and TVET students. It is designed to provide instant, unlimited access to a variety of services related to the funding of higher education. By utilizing this system, students can manage their financial requirements without the need for manual, paper-based processes for many routine tasks.

Who Can Use the Portal?

Access to the Student Portal is available to any registered existing student. The service is provided freely, allowing users to log in at their convenience to monitor the status of their accounts and handle administrative tasks related to their loans.

Key Features and Functions

The portal simplifies the user experience by offering a comprehensive range of self-service tools. Once registered and logged in, you can access information regarding the lifecycle of your HELB loan, including the application process, the specific allocation of funds, and the current status of your disbursements.

Beyond basic account monitoring, the portal is an essential tool for managing your financial commitments. It provides a platform to address tasks such as loan repayment and compliance. Because HELB provides a range of products and services, the portal serves as a consistent interface where students can interact with the board for various institutional requirements.

How to Access the Service

To begin using the portal, you must first register for an account. If you are already a registered user, you can log in directly using your credentials. The system is maintained as a user-friendly platform, intended to make the management of educational funding more efficient for students across the country.

Important Resources and Support

For students requiring additional information, the portal includes sections for Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) and direct contact channels. HELB also provides alternative methods for students to interact with their services, including the USSD code *642# and the official HELB Mobile App. 

Students are encouraged to maintain their account security and keep their login information private. If you have questions about specific eligibility criteria, application deadlines, or specific financial amounts, please verify these details directly on the official HELB website at https://www.helb.co.ke/online-services/student-portal/. Avoid relying on third-party sources for sensitive account information to ensure the accuracy and security of your data.

title: HELB Loans
summary: Understanding Higher Education Loans Board Loans
content:
Understanding Higher Education Loans Board Loans

For students across Kenya, navigating the financial requirements of higher education is a significant undertaking. The Higher Education Loans Board, commonly known as HELB, is the primary body tasked with providing financial assistance to students in universities, colleges, and TVET institutions. Understanding the nature of these loans and how to interact with the system is essential for any student seeking to support their academic journey.

What HELB Loans Are

HELB loans are financial products designed to assist eligible Kenyan students in meeting the costs of their education. These loans are provided to ensure that students can access higher learning opportunities regardless of their immediate financial background. Because these are loan products, they are governed by specific terms and conditions that borrowers must understand, particularly regarding repayment obligations.

Key Portals for Students and Stakeholders

To manage the loan lifecycle, HELB utilizes an integrated digital ecosystem. Students should become familiar with the official HELB student portal, which serves as the primary gateway for applications, account management, and status updates. Beyond the student portal, HELB maintains specific digital interfaces for other stakeholders to ensure transparency and proper management of loan records. These include separate portals dedicated to loanees, educational institutions, employers, and debt collectors. By centralizing these services online, HELB aims to streamline the process of disbursement and monitoring.

Maintaining Compliance and Getting Support

Managing a HELB account goes beyond the initial application. Students and beneficiaries should be aware of the importance of maintaining compliance throughout their loan journey. The official HELB website provides resources for those needing a compliance certificate, which is a critical document for many graduates entering the workforce. 

If you encounter technical issues or have specific questions regarding your loan, you should utilize the official Get-In-Touch resources provided on the HELB website. This ensures that you are communicating directly with the board through verified channels rather than relying on unofficial sources. Additionally, the HELB website offers a Self-Serve platform that allows users to manage various aspects of their accounts independently.

Staying Informed

As a student, it is your responsibility to stay informed about the latest updates from the Higher Education Loans Board. Because policies and procedural requirements can be subject to change, always prioritize information found directly on the official HELB website at helb.co.ke. 

If you are currently enrolled or preparing to join a tertiary institution, you should check the official portal frequently for any announcements, application deadlines, or updates to your student account status. While third-party platforms may discuss student funding, only the official HELB website and their verified social media channels, such as their Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, and LinkedIn pages, should be treated as the authoritative source for your financial aid information. By maintaining a professional relationship with the board through these official channels, you ensure that you remain in good standing throughout your academic career and beyond.

title: TVET Loans - HELB
summary: TVET Loans - HELB
content:
TVET Loans - HELB

Overview of TVET Loans
The Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) provides financial support to students enrolled in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutions. This program is designed to assist students in meeting the costs of their technical education.

Application Requirements
To apply as a first-time applicant, you must adhere to the official procedures provided by HELB. You need a valid National ID. If you do not possess one, you must have your KCSE index number. You will also require a valid email address and a functional telephone number to receive a verification code during the registration process.

How to Apply
The application process is conducted through the official Student Portal. First, visit the website hef.co.ke and click on register to create your account. Enter your National ID number or KCSE index number as required. Once you provide your email address, you will receive a notification to activate your account; check your inbox, spam, or junk folders if you do not see it immediately. After activation, log in and provide a valid telephone number to receive a verification code.

Once your account is verified, fill in your profile and update your biodata. You must read and consent to the collection of your personal data by checking the appropriate box. Complete the form with your personal details and save your progress. Before submission, ensure you update your guarantor details and provide the necessary loan payment information, which includes bank and mobile payment details. Finally, accept the loan terms and conditions to consent to the processing of your data and submit your application.

What Students Should Do Now
If you are a student seeking funding, the primary step is to access the official HELB portal at hef.co.ke. Follow the steps outlined above to ensure your application is complete. Because HELB procedures and requirements can be updated, you should always verify specific deadlines, eligibility details, or potential changes to the application process directly on the official HELB website. Do not rely on third-party information; always confirm details through the official channels provided by HELB to ensure your application is accurate and successful.

title: Undergraduate Loans - HELB
summary: UNDERGRADUATE LOANS: HELB GUIDELINES
content:
UNDERGRADUATE LOANS: HELB GUIDELINES

The Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) provides financial support to students pursuing Bachelor’s degrees. This support is intended for students enrolled in Public and Chartered Private Universities within the East African Community. Eligibility covers students placed through the Kenya Universities and Colleges Central Placement Service (KUCCPS) as well as self-sponsored, parallel, and Module II students. Please note that pre-university, certificate, diploma, and postgraduate students are not eligible to apply for this specific loan.

KEY LOAN DETAILS

These loans are interest-bearing, currently set at a rate of 4% per annum, and include an annual ledger fee of Kshs. 1,000. The duration of loan eligibility is tied directly to the length of your academic program. For example, a student enrolled in a four-year degree program is eligible for four years of funding, while a five-year program qualifies for five years of support. 

APPLICATION TYPES

There are two primary categories for loan applications: 
First-time applicants are those applying for the initial year of their degree program. 
Second and subsequent applicants are those returning to the board for their second, third, or fourth year of study, depending on the remaining duration of their course.

HOW TO APPLY

Students are advised to initiate their application at least one month before the academic term begins to ensure sufficient processing time. To apply, you must visit the official HELB student portal at hef.co.ke. Once on the site, click on the register option to create your personal account and follow the on-screen instructions to complete your application. 

IMPORTANT STUDENT ADVISORY

If you are uncertain about specific documentation requirements, deadlines, or further eligibility criteria not explicitly detailed here, you should verify all information directly through the official HELB website at https://www.helb.co.ke/helb-products/helb-loans/undergraduate-loans/. Always rely on official portal communications for your specific application status.

1. Overview of the application route

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program continues to use a partner-based application model for Kenyan students. The official where-to-apply page on the Mastercard Foundation website lists where applicants should apply and directs students to the relevant partner universities and non-governmental organizations that offer scholarship opportunities. It is an official Mastercard Foundation program page for the Scholars Program, but it is not a single central application portal for every applicant.

For Kenyan students, this means the Mastercard Foundation page should be treated as an official gateway and navigation page rather than a complete scholarship notice. A student must first identify a participating institution, then follow that institution’s own scholarship or admissions process exactly as published. The Foundation’s guidance directs applicants to the relevant partner institution rather than collecting every application in one place.

The page is current and was updated on 2026-09-08, which confirms it remains relevant for present applicants. That current status matters because partner routes, open calls, and application instructions can change from cycle to cycle.

2. What the current update confirms

The verified information for this page confirms three core facts. First, the page lists where Kenyan students can apply for Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program opportunities. Second, it is an official Mastercard Foundation program page for the Scholars Program. Third, the page was recently updated on 2026-09-08.

What remains unchanged is the decentralized structure of the program. The Foundation page is the entry point, but the actual scholarship application rules are handled by each partner institution. Kenyan applicants should therefore continue to rely on the institution-specific call for applications, admissions page, or scholarship page for the most accurate instructions.

This distinction is important for students who may assume that one application form works everywhere. For this scholarship, the Foundation provides direction, but the partner institution controls the actual application process, deadlines, and selection steps.

3. Who this guidance applies to

This guidance applies to students seeking consideration through the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program via partner institutions, including Kenyan students. The page is designed to help applicants locate the institution offering the scholarship opportunity and move to the correct application route.

Because the program is decentralized, eligibility is not identical across all partners. A Kenyan student may qualify for one opportunity and not another depending on the level of study, academic program, citizenship or residency conditions, financial need criteria, leadership expectations, or other requirements set by that specific institution. The Foundation page does not publish one shared eligibility list for every applicant.

That distinction matters for students comparing opportunities. The official where-to-apply page identifies where to apply; it does not replace the individual partner’s scholarship notice, admissions page, or call for applications. Students should always read the partner institution’s current notice before taking any action.

4. How the application process works

The application process begins with the partner institution the student wants to attend. The official guidance directs applicants to apply through the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program-affiliated institution they wish to attend. In practice, that means the student must find a participating university or organization first, then open that institution’s scholarship page, admissions page, or dedicated application announcement.

This structure means the process can differ widely between institutions. Some partners may ask students to apply for admission first and then be considered for scholarship support. Others may issue a separate scholarship form or a dedicated call for applications. Some may include interviews, screening, or shortlisting before final selection. Kenyan applicants should therefore read the entire opportunity notice carefully before starting.

Submission methods also vary by partner. One institution may use an online form, while another may require documents to be sent by email or submitted through another channel stated on the institution’s own site. The Foundation page does not standardize these procedures across all partners, so applicants should not assume that one institution’s process applies to another.

For Kenyan students, the partner page is the authoritative source for requirements. One opportunity may require a particular degree level or academic threshold. Another may emphasize financial need, leadership potential, community service, or a specific field of study. The final and correct source for all requirements is always the individual institution’s scholarship or admissions page.

Students should also confirm whether the scholarship is tied to a specific program, school, faculty, or admission round. Some opportunities may require a separate admissions application before scholarship consideration, while others may combine both steps. If the institution publishes separate instructions, those instructions should be followed exactly.

Instead, deadlines are set by each partner institution. Some opportunities may be open now, while others may not yet be posted or may already be closed for the current cycle. Timing can also vary by academic year, degree level, and institutional calendar.

For Kenyan applicants, the most reliable approach is to check the specific institution’s official website before preparing an application. Students should not wait for a Foundation-wide deadline announcement, because the controlling date is the one published by the partner institution. The official guidance page itself does not provide a universal expiry date or reopening date.

- Locate the scholarship notice, admissions page, or Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program page.

- Submit the application exactly as instructed by the institution.

This is the safest method because each partner institution manages its own process. Kenyan students should avoid relying only on third-party summaries or informal notices, since those may not reflect the latest instructions.

Students should pay close attention to whether the partner institution is currently accepting applications. The official Mastercard Foundation page points applicants to the correct institution, but it does not announce one opening or closing date for every opportunity.

It is also important to compare institutions carefully. Different partners may offer different academic programs, application requirements, and selection processes. Another key point is that the official page was updated on 2026-09-08. That confirms the partner-application guidance is current and relevant for present applicants. Even so, the final rules always live on the partner institution’s own page, which should be checked immediately before applying.

title: Mauritius – Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS) 2026: What Kenyan Students Need to Know
summary: The Ministry of Education has published a 2026 call for applications for the Mauritius – Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS), an international scholarship opportunity for Kenyan students. The scheme is aimed at undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral study in Mauritius, and the official notice says successful candidates may receive support toward tuition fees and living expenses. Interested applicants must obtain the official Standard Application Forms from the Ministry of Education offices at Telposta Towers or download them from the Ministry website, then submit the required documents by the stated deadline. Students should carefully check the official notice and prepare their applications early because the Ministry has set a clear closing date.
content:
## 1. What This Announcement Is About
The Ministry of Education has issued a 2026 call for applications for the Mauritius – Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS) 2026. This is an international scholarship opportunity for Kenyan students who want to study in Mauritius. The official notice says the scheme is offered by the Government of the Republic of Mauritius and is intended for study at undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral levels.

For Kenyan university, college, and TVET students who are planning further study abroad, this announcement matters because it is an official government scholarship call and not a general education notice. It provides a structured route for eligible applicants to compete for places in Mauritius for the 2026 academic intake.

## 2. Who Is Affected
This announcement affects Kenyan students who want to apply for an overseas scholarship under the Mauritius – Africa Scholarship Scheme 2026. The official notice states that the scholarship is open to candidates at undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral levels.

The notice also shows that the scheme is relevant to students who can meet the conditions set out in the application call and who are able to submit the required documents to the Ministry of Education in Kenya. Because the scholarship is advertised through the Ministry’s official scholarships listing, Kenyan applicants should treat the Ministry as the main channel for application guidance and submission.

## 3. The Important Information
The official notice states that the Government of the Republic of Mauritius is offering fifteen (15) scholarships to Kenyan students for the 2026 academic intake. The scholarships are tenable in various universities in Mauritius.

The notice also says the scholarship will support successful candidates in meeting their tuition fees and contributing to their living expenses during their studies in Mauritius. That means the award is not simply an admission notice; it is a funded scholarship opportunity with support for study costs and basic living expenses, subject to selection.

The application process has both an online and a physical component. Applicants are required to apply electronically by filling the official application form available on the Mauritius scholarship portal before printing. In addition, they must obtain Standard Application Forms from the Ministry of Education offices at Telposta Towers, 27th Floor, Room 2702, or download them from the Ministry’s website.

The notice further states that completed forms and supporting documents must be sent to the Director – Higher Education, Ministry of Education, P. O. Box 9583 – 00200, Nairobi, or delivered to the Telposta Towers office.

## 4. Eligibility or Requirements
The official notice includes specific conditions for different study levels, but the details shown in the available notice are incomplete in this summary. What is clear is that the scholarship has separate conditions for undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral applicants.

For undergraduate applicants, the notice states the following requirements:
- Minimum KCSE Mean Grade of B (plain)
- Not more than 25 years of age
- Strong grades in major subjects relevant to the preferred programme
- Completed secondary education in the last three (3) years
- Have an original KCSE certificate

The notice also shows that post-secondary applicants must meet additional conditions tied to their level and study background. Because the official PDF contains more detailed criteria for master’s and doctoral applicants, students should read the full notice carefully before applying and confirm that they meet the stated requirements for their specific level.

## 5. Important Dates and Deadlines
The official deadline stated in the notice is 23rd February 2026. The application forms must reach the Ministry not later than that date.

This is the most important date in the announcement. Students should not wait until the last minute, because the process requires both online completion and submission of printed documents. Late applications would likely not be considered if they arrive after the deadline.

## 6. How Students Can Apply or Access the Service
Students should follow these steps:

- Go to the official Mauritius scholarship application portal and complete the online application form.
- Print the completed online form after filling it electronically.
- Obtain the Standard Application Forms from the Ministry of Education offices at Telposta Towers, 27th Floor, Room 2702, or download them from the Ministry’s website.
- Prepare the required supporting documents listed in the notice, including certified photocopies of the birth certificate and ID, certified academic or professional certificates, transcripts, evidence of application for enrolment in a public higher education institution in Mauritius, and other testimonials.
- Submit two completed copies of the online application form together with the required documents to the Director – Higher Education, Ministry of Education, P. O. Box 9583 – 00200, Nairobi, or deliver them to Telposta Towers, 27th Floor, Room 2702.

Students should make sure all copies are complete and certified where required, because incomplete applications may not be processed properly.

## 7. What Students Should Do Now
Students who are interested in this scholarship should act immediately if they have not already done so. The first step is to read the official notice carefully so they understand the level-specific requirements and the documents needed.

They should then confirm whether they meet the academic and age conditions stated in the notice, especially undergraduate applicants who must meet the KCSE and age thresholds. After that, they should begin gathering certified documents, since these often take time to prepare.

Students should also use the official application portal and the Ministry’s official website rather than relying on shared copies or unofficial summaries. Since the notice is hosted on the Ministry of Education scholarships listing, students should treat that page and the official PDF as the authoritative sources.

## 8. Important Things to Remember
The scholarship is an official 2026 government call, so students should rely only on the terms in the notice.

The notice clearly states that the scholarship supports tuition fees and living expenses, but it does not provide every detail in the summary available here, so applicants should verify the full conditions before submitting.

The deadline is fixed, and the application must reach the Ministry by 23rd February 2026.

Applicants should not assume eligibility based on general academic strength alone; they must meet the specific requirements for their level of study and provide all the documents listed in the notice.

Official source: Ministry of Education, Kenya — Mauritius – Africa Scholarship Scheme (MASS) 2026 notice and scholarships listing.
